stories.title: Wall Street funds add nearly $90M to altcoins as XRP, SOL, and HYPE rise
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that institutional buyers added close to $90 million into altcoin positions, alongside gains in XRP, SOL, and HYPE. The figure comes from one report covering a short window. Treat it as a snapshot, not a confirmed trend.
stories.whyItMatters: Institutional buying in altcoins can shape retail sentiment and flows beyond Bitcoin and Ethereum.
whatToWatch: Whether altcoin inflows continue past this week
Confirmation from other flow trackers or exchanges
questions: Which specific funds made these purchases?
Is the $90M figure net of outflows or gross buying only?

sources.title: Wall Street just poured nearly $90 million into altcoins as XRP, SOL and HYPE rip higher

stories.title: Term Finance loses an estimated $8.5M in vault governance exploit
stories.summary: Attackers exploited a governance weakness in Term Finance's vault system and drained an estimated $8.5 million, Cointelegraph reports. The exact exploit mechanism is not detailed in the initial report. Term Finance is a DeFi lending protocol.
stories.whyItMatters: Governance-layer exploits show attackers keep finding weaknesses beyond smart-contract code, raising the risk bar for DeFi depositors.
whatToWatch: An official post-mortem from Term Finance
Whether any funds can be recovered or frozen
Comment from auditors who reviewed the vault
questions: What governance mechanism was exploited?
Will affected users get compensation?

sources.title: Term Finance loses estimated $8.5M in vault governance exploit

stories.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs post their biggest weekly inflows of 2026
stories.summary: US spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs recorded their largest combined weekly inflows of 2026 so far, CryptoSlate reports. The inflows coincided with a broader crypto price rally. The report presents the inflows as accompanying the rally, not proven to have caused it.
stories.whyItMatters: Large ETF inflows are a clearer signal of institutional demand than short-term price swings.
whatToWatch: Whether inflows hold up or reverse next week
Fund-level flow data from individual issuers
questions: How much of the inflow is new money versus rotation from other products?

sources.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs just had their biggest week of 2026 as crypto exploded higher

stories.title: US allows high-leverage Bitcoin trading as crypto founders stay blocked from raising funds
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that US regulators approved high-leverage Bitcoin trading products, even as crypto startup founders remain legally restricted from raising capital domestically. The piece contrasts rules for trading infrastructure with rules for company formation.
stories.whyItMatters: The contrast shows an uneven approach: easier access to leveraged speculation, harder access to capital for builders.
whatToWatch: Any legislative or SEC action on founder fundraising restrictions
Uptake of the new leverage product and any resulting risk incidents
questions: Which specific leverage product and venue got approval?
What rule blocks founder fundraising?

sources.title: The US approved high-leverage Bitcoin trading while crypto founders remain legally blocked from raising funds

stories.title: CoinDesk's State of Crypto: regulation has arrived
stories.summary: CoinDesk's State of Crypto column argues that crypto regulation is now a present reality, not a future prospect. This is framed as analysis, not a single reported event. The title alone gives no further specifics.
stories.whyItMatters: Tracking how commentators frame the regulatory shift helps readers read the broader narrative, even from one column.
whatToWatch: Future State of Crypto columns for specific rule changes
Any concrete rulemaking that follows this framing
questions: What specific regulatory actions does the column cite as evidence?

stories.title: Crypto card spending passes $1 billion as stablecoins spread into daily payments
stories.summary: CoinDesk reports crypto card spending has passed $1 billion, with stablecoins increasingly used for everyday purchases. A companion CoinDesk piece points to AI agents as a growing category of stablecoin users. Separately, CryptoSlate reports a crypto treasury firm is seeking a 20 billion share ceiling and reverse splits after a $300 million stock offering.
stories.whyItMatters: Stablecoins moving into routine spending, including by automated agents, is a concrete adoption signal, more telling than price speculation.
whatToWatch: Growth of crypto card spending in coming quarters
How AI-agent stablecoin payments scale in practice
Outcome of the treasury firm's share ceiling and reverse split plans
questions: Which stablecoins and card issuers make up most of the $1B figure?
What business underlies the treasury firm's capital raise?

stories.title: Bitcoin's 23% rally tied to US debt policy: Cointelegraph's weekly digest
stories.summary: Cointelegraph's Hodler's Digest recaps a week in which Bitcoin rallied 23%, which the piece links to US debt policy developments. As a weekly roundup, it compiles multiple stories rather than one discrete event. Treat the stated rally driver as the outlet's framing, not a confirmed cause.
stories.whyItMatters: Sharp rallies tied to macro policy are worth tracking, but roundup framing can overstate one cause behind a multi-factor price move.
whatToWatch: Whether the rally holds beyond the reported week
Any specific US debt policy action driving sentiment
questions: What specific debt policy event is being credited?
Does the 23% figure cover one week or a longer span?

stories.title: Bitcoin Core weighs dropping encrypted routing support amid eclipse-attack risk
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports that Bitcoin Core developers are considering dropping support for encrypted routing. They cite poor overall node health that leaves users exposed to eclipse attacks. An eclipse attack isolates a node from the honest network to feed it false data.
stories.whyItMatters: Changes to Bitcoin's networking layer affect node operators' security directly, and eclipse-attack exposure undermines trust in the data nodes see.
whatToWatch: The outcome of the Bitcoin Core developer discussion
Any proposed fix for node health short of removing the feature
Timeline for a decision or code change
questions: Why has node health declined enough to prompt this debate?
What replaces encrypted routing if it is dropped?

sources.title: Bitcoin Core considers dropping encrypted routing support as poor node health exposes users to eclipse attacks

stories.title: Tokenization's next phase is about utility, not just issuance
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate piece argues that tokenization is entering a phase focused on real utility, not simply issuing tokenized assets. The title points to an analysis piece rather than one reported event. No further specifics are given.
stories.whyItMatters: A shift toward utility-focused tokenization would mark a maturing market moving past pilot announcements toward actual use.
whatToWatch: Specific utility-focused tokenization projects the piece may cite
Whether other outlets adopt the same framing
questions: What concrete examples define 'utility' here?

sources.title: The next phase of tokenization is utility

stories.title: Fed study: crypto investors act on beliefs, sway easily with returns
stories.summary: A Federal Reserve study, reported by Cointelegraph, finds crypto investors are driven mainly by personal beliefs. It finds they shift behavior easily in response to returns. The finding suggests sentiment and recent performance play an outsized role in decisions.
stories.whyItMatters: A Fed-backed look at investor psychology adds weight to skepticism about price-driven hype in this market.
whatToWatch: Full publication of the study's methodology and data
Any policy commentary the Fed draws from the findings
questions: What data set and sample size underlie the study?
Does the study separate retail from institutional investors?

sources.title: Fed study finds crypto investors driven by beliefs, easily swayed by returns

stories.title: Bitcoin miner's IPO gives public buyers 10% equity for 99.8% of funds raised
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports a Bitcoin mining company's IPO structure asks public investors to supply 99.8% of the capital raised. In return, they receive only 10% of the resulting equity. The report frames this as a notably lopsided arrangement compared with typical IPO terms.
stories.whyItMatters: This kind of skewed IPO structure is a signal investors should scrutinize before treating crypto-adjacent listings as straightforward equity exposure.
whatToWatch: Whether the IPO proceeds as structured or gets amended
Investor and regulator reaction to the equity split
Subscription demand at these terms
questions: Which miner and exchange are involved?
Why would investors accept these terms?

sources.title: Bitcoin miner IPO demands 99.8% of funds from public buyers while handing them just 10% equity

stories.title: $20M crypto payout leaves micro-cap firm with under $83K in usable cash
stories.summary: CryptoSlate reports a micro-cap company received a $20 million crypto-related payout, yet ended up with under $83,000 in usable cash reserves. This suggests the payout was largely non-cash, restricted, or otherwise not immediately accessible. The exact reason is not detailed in the title.
stories.whyItMatters: The gap between a headline payout and actual usable cash is a reminder to look past reported crypto windfalls at small-cap firms.
whatToWatch: The firm's next financial filing for clarity on the payout structure
Whether the firm raises additional capital soon
questions: Why is so little of the $20M usable cash?
Which firm and what asset made up the payout?

sources.title: How a $20M crypto payout left a micro-cap firm with under $83K in usable cash reserves
